summary: Luke Badiali reviewed five recent proposals with Chris and Leanne. Discovery is thin, qualification is informal and proposals are long and methodology heavy. We agreed a structured discovery call with the operating partner and a shorter proposal format.

discussion.keyPoints: Two of the five losses came after 30-page proposals that never mentioned the investment case. Chris accepted the proposals were written for plant managers, not operating partners.
Discovery calls are usually with the plant manager. Leanne said they rarely ask about the hold period or the exit plan.
There is no shared definition of a qualified opportunity, so partners spend time on proposals that were never likely to close.

recommendations.recommendation: Every discovery includes the operating partner and covers 6 set questions, including hold period, EBITDA target and exit timing.
Cap proposals at 8 pages, opening with the EBITDA bridge from the investment case.
Adopt a simple scoring of budget owner, value-creation plan link and start date; do not write a proposal below 2 out of 3.
Run a monthly pitch review where Leanne coaches partners on two live opportunities.

actions.action: Rewrite the proposal template to the 8-page format

nextFocus: Define pipeline stages and exit criteria to match the new process.
nextPreparation: Leanne to export all open opportunities with stage and value.

tests.question: What did we agree about proposal length?
Is the qualification scoring agreed yet?
Who needs to be on discovery calls?
